name.text: Locus of the midpoints of equal chords

questiontext.text:
A circle has centre \(O\) and radius \({@r@}\) cm.

(a) Chords of length \({@c@}\) cm are drawn in the circle. Find the radius of the locus of their midpoints, correct to 1 decimal place where it is not a whole number.

[[input:ans1]] cm [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) For each chord length, choose the locus of the midpoints of all chords of that length.

  1. Chords of length \({@cl[pm[1]]@}\) cm [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
  2. Chords of length \({@cl[pm[2]]@}\) cm [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
  3. Chords of length \({@cl[pm[3]]@}\) cm [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) The perpendicular from \(O\) to a chord bisects it. If \(M\) is the midpoint of a chord \(AB\) of length \({@c@}\) cm, then \(AM = {@c/2@}\) cm and triangle \(OMA\) has a right angle at \(M\):

\[OM^2 = OA^2 - AM^2 = {@r@}^2 - {@c/2@}^2 = {@r^2-c^2/4@}\]

[[if test="integerp(rm)"]]So \(OM = {@rm@}\) cm[[else]]So \(OM = \sqrt{ {@r^2-c^2/4@} } \approx {@dispdp(float(floor(10^1*(rm)+1/2)/10^1),1)@}\) cm[[/if]] for every such chord: the midpoints lie on the circle with centre \(O\) and that radius.

(b)

  • [[if test="is(pm[1]=1)"]]A chord of {@c2@} cm is shorter than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so such chords exist and none passes through O: their midpoints are all \(\sqrt{ {@r@}^2 - {@c2/2@}^2 }\) cm from \(O\), on a circle with centre \(O\).[[elif test="is(pm[1]=2)"]]A chord of {@2*r@} cm is a diameter, so every one has its midpoint at \(O\).[[else]]No chord can be longer than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so there are no chords of {@c3@} cm.[[/if]]

  • [[if test="is(pm[2]=1)"]]A chord of {@c2@} cm is shorter than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so such chords exist and none passes through O: their midpoints are all \(\sqrt{ {@r@}^2 - {@c2/2@}^2 }\) cm from \(O\), on a circle with centre \(O\).[[elif test="is(pm[2]=2)"]]A chord of {@2*r@} cm is a diameter, so every one has its midpoint at \(O\).[[else]]No chord can be longer than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so there are no chords of {@c3@} cm.[[/if]]

  • [[if test="is(pm[3]=1)"]]A chord of {@c2@} cm is shorter than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so such chords exist and none passes through O: their midpoints are all \(\sqrt{ {@r@}^2 - {@c2/2@}^2 }\) cm from \(O\), on a circle with centre \(O\).[[elif test="is(pm[3]=2)"]]A chord of {@2*r@} cm is a diameter, so every one has its midpoint at \(O\).[[else]]No chord can be longer than the diameter, {@2*r@} cm, so there are no chords of {@c3@} cm.[[/if]]

questionnote.text: r={@r@}, c={@c@}, locus radius={@dispdp(float(floor(10^1*(rm)+1/2)/10^1),1)@}, sw={@sw@}, c2={@c2@}, c3={@c3@}, order {@pm@}

questiondescription.text:
Loci: locus of the midpoints of equal chords

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.3 (loci involving chords): Find the radius of the locus of the midpoints of equal chords, and decide when the locus is a circle, a point or empty.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: You used the whole chord, \({@c@}\) cm, in Pythagoras. The right-angled triangle is \(OMA\), where \(M\) is the midpoint of the chord \(AB\): how long is \(AM\)?
\({@r@} - {@c/2@} = {@r-c/2@}\) subtracts the lengths. Pythagoras in triangle \(OMA\) works with the squares of the sides.
That is half the chord, \(AM\). You need \(OM\), from the centre to the midpoint.

falsefeedback.text: The perpendicular from \(O\) bisects the chord, so triangle \(OMA\) has a right angle at the midpoint \(M\). With \(OM = {@ans1@}\), \(OM^2 + AM^2\) would be [[if test="integerp(ans1)"]]\({@ans1^2+c^2/4@}\)[[else]]about \({@dispdp(float(ans1^2+c^2/4),2)@}\)[[/if]], but \(OA^2 = {@r@}^2 = {@r^2@}\).

node.description: Row diagnostic: shorter chord given the point, diameter or too-long chord given a circle

truefeedback.text: [[if test="is(ans2=\"pt\")"]]If every midpoint were at \(O\), every such chord would pass through the centre, and a chord through the centre is a diameter, \({@2*r@}\) cm long. These chords are \({@cl[pm[1]]@}\) cm long.[[elif test="is(ans2=\"circ\")"]]A circle of midpoints needs chords that exist and whose midpoints are all the same distance, more than zero, from \(O\). Try to draw one chord of \({@cl[pm[1]]@}\) cm in a circle whose diameter is \({@2*r@}\) cm: can you, and where is its midpoint?[[else]]There are no such chords only when the length is more than the longest chord the circle has. The longest chord is the diameter, \({@2*r@}\) cm: compare it with \({@cl[pm[1]]@}\) cm.[[/if]]
